nonClaims: No real main proof was run: the tool never ran against a real merge commit; the execution branch is proven only with fake steps in a throwaway repository and the dry-run pins.

The exact-main-ladder step was never run for real: no Playwright run, no smoke rerun, no port or server check; its argv and log/hash recording are pinned, its runtime cost is the U9 figure quoted in the admission, not a new measurement.

npm's own script execution is outside the seam: build (a package script chain) and openspec-strict (npx resolving the global openspec bin) still pass through npm's script shell inside npm; their argv are fixed literals, and no caller-provided text reaches them.
resolveArgv's POSIX candidate (../lib/node_modules/npm/bin) was not exercised on a POSIX machine; only the Windows layout was measured here.
The tool exit code still does not follow step exits (unchanged by design, see admission failsClosed).

findingsReportedNotFixed.text: The sha256 step runs before restore-next-env, so on a fresh log directory restore-next-env.log is never hashed, and sha256.txt hashes every .log present, including logs a previous attempt left in the same directory: u37-main-proof-20260925/sha256.txt lists restore-next-env.log (f891db..., the same bytes as tsc.log), which one run of the ladder in its own order does not write before the sha256 step (INFERENCE: an earlier attempt in the same directory left it). The fake-step pin asserts every listed digest and the step logs before sha256, not the absence of restore-next-env.

runExactMainLadder --rerun returns SATISFIED without rerunning when the evidence or archive dir already covers the sha, so a second proof attempt on the same merge commit reuses the first attempt's smoke run instead of rerunning it.

An empty --runtime-jest '' passes the exactly-one check but is falsy, so it falls through to the --runtime-command branch and is refused RUNTIME_COMMAND_NOT_ARGV (fails closed, with a message naming the wrong flag).
